topics.name: Installing Rocky Linux 9 in VirtualBox
watch: How to download and install Rocky Linux 9 on VirtualBox (step by step)
read: Rocky Linux docs: Installing Rocky Linux 9
Rocky Linux docs: Rocky on VirtualBox
practice: Red Hat free interactive labs (RHEL in your browser)
topics.ai_job: Admins use AI to troubleshoot install errors: paste the exact error (for example “no bootable medium”) and ask for the likely cause and fix. AI can also suggest VM sizes for a lab or a small server.
prompts: I'm installing Rocky Linux 9 minimal in VirtualBox on Windows with 4 GB RAM, 2 CPUs and a 40 GB disk. Explain each installer screen in simple words and what I should choose.
What is the difference between a physical server, a virtual machine and a container? Explain with a real-life example.
interview: What is a virtual machine and why do companies use them?
What is the difference between RHEL, Rocky Linux and CentOS?
What happens when a Linux server boots, in simple steps?

topics.name: First look at your server: hostnamectl, uname -r, /etc/os-release, df -h
watch: Learn Linux TV: uname command simplified (in Linux Crash Course)
read: Rocky Linux book: Introduction to Linux
topics.ai_job: On the job, you paste command output (like df -h) into AI and ask “is anything wrong here?”. AI quickly spots a disk that is almost full or an old kernel.
prompts: I ran hostnamectl, uname -r, cat /etc/os-release and df -h on my new Rocky Linux server. Here is the output: [paste]. Explain every line in simple words.
Which 5 commands should a Linux admin run first on a new server to understand it? Explain why for each.
interview: How do you check which Linux version and kernel a server is running?
How do you check free disk space? What does df -h show?

topics.name: Changing the hostname (hostnamectl)
watch: Learn Linux TV: Linux Commands for Beginners (playlist)
read: Red Hat docs (RHEL 9): Changing a hostname
Red Hat blog: How to change your hostname in Linux
practice: Red Hat free interactive labs (RHEL in your browser)
topics.ai_job: In real jobs admins rename many servers at once. AI can write an Ansible playbook or a small script that sets hostnames on 50 servers from a list, which saves hours.
prompts: Explain static, transient and pretty hostnames on Rocky Linux 9 with one simple example each.
Write a small Ansible playbook that sets the hostname of 3 servers from a list. Explain each line.
interview: How do you change a server's hostname permanently?
Where is the hostname stored on RHEL/Rocky Linux?

topics.name: The shell prompt and logging in again
watch: Learn Linux TV: Linux Crash Course (playlist)
topics.ai_job: Admins ask AI to customise their prompt (show the time, the folder or a red colour for root), so they always know which server they are on and don't run commands on the wrong one.
prompts: Explain my Linux prompt [hemanth@server1 ~]$ part by part.
How can I change my Bash prompt to show the time and turn red when I am root? Give the steps.
interview: What is the difference between $ and # in the prompt?
What is a shell? Name two shells.

topics.name: The /etc folder and /etc/os-release
watch: freeCodeCamp: Introduction to Linux, full course
practice: OverTheWire Bandit: learn commands as a game
topics.ai_job: Before editing a config file, admins paste it into AI and ask what each setting does. AI can also write scripts that read /etc/os-release to install the right packages on different Linux versions.
prompts: I ran ls -l /etc. Explain the 10 most important files for a Linux admin in simple words.
What does ID_LIKE mean in /etc/os-release, and why is it useful in scripts?
interview: What is stored in /etc?
Name 3 important files in /etc and what they do.

topics.name: /var and /var/log: where logs live
watch: Learn How to Access and Read Linux Log Files
topics.ai_job: Reading logs is a big part of an admin's day. AI helps you understand confusing log lines: paste 20 lines and ask what went wrong and what to check next.
prompts: Here are 20 lines from /var/log/messages on my Rocky Linux server: [paste]. Explain what happened in simple words and tell me if anything is wrong.
What kinds of files are stored in /var, and why is it kept separate from /etc?
interview: Where are system logs stored on Linux?
What is the difference between /var/log/messages and /var/log/secure?

topics.name: tail, tail -f and journalctl
watch: Learn Linux TV: journalctl Basics: How to Easily Check Your Linux Logs
read: Red Hat docs (RHEL 9): Troubleshooting problems by using log files
practice: Red Hat free interactive labs (RHEL in your browser)
topics.ai_job: When a service breaks, admins watch logs live (tail -f or journalctl -f) and ask AI to explain the error message and suggest a fix. AI can also build the right journalctl filter, for example “only errors from sshd since yesterday”.
prompts: Give me 5 useful journalctl commands for a beginner admin and explain when to use each.
What is the difference between tail -f and journalctl -f?
interview: How do you watch a log file live?
How do you see logs for one service with journalctl?

topics.name: Making folders and files: mkdir, touch, cp, mv, rm
watch: Learn Linux TV: Touch Command Made Easy (in Linux Crash Course)
practice: OverTheWire Bandit: learn commands as a game
topics.ai_job: Admins use AI to write safe one-line commands, like “copy all .conf files to a backup folder with today's date”, and to double-check a dangerous rm command before running it.
prompts: Explain mkdir -p, cp -r, mv and rm -r with a simple example of each. Which one is dangerous and why?
Before I run this command, tell me exactly what it will delete: [paste command]
interview: What is the difference between cp and mv?
Why is rm -rf dangerous? How do you stay safe?

topics.name: Hidden files and ls -la
watch: Learn Linux TV: Linux Commands for Beginners (playlist)
practice: OverTheWire Bandit: learn commands as a game
topics.ai_job: AI can explain every column of ls -la (permissions, owner, size, date) so you can quickly read a folder you have never seen on a new server.
prompts: Explain every column in the output of ls -la using this example: [paste]
What are hidden files in Linux, and which ones in my home folder are important?
interview: How do you show hidden files?
What do the 10 characters like -rw-r--r-- mean?

topics.name: find: finding files
watch: Learn Linux TV: Linux Crash Course (playlist)
read: Rocky Linux book: Advanced Linux Commands
practice: OverTheWire Bandit: learn commands as a game
topics.ai_job: Admins ask AI to build find commands for cleanup, for example “files bigger than 1 GB, older than 30 days, in /var”. AI writes the command and explains each part.
prompts: Write a find command that lists files bigger than 100 MB in /var, and explain each part.
Give me 5 useful find examples for a Linux admin.
interview: How do you find all .conf files under /etc?
How do you find large files that fill up a disk?

topics.name: grep: searching inside files
watch: freeCodeCamp: Introduction to Linux, full course
read: Ryan's Tutorials: Grep and Regular Expressions
practice: OverTheWire Bandit: learn commands as a game
topics.ai_job: grep is used every day to search logs. AI helps you write grep patterns, for example “find all failed SSH logins and count them by IP address”.
prompts: Explain grep -i, -r, -n and -v with one example each.
Write a command that finds failed SSH login attempts in /var/log/secure and counts them by IP address.
interview: How do you search for a word inside all files in a folder?
What does grep -v do?

topics.name: which, whereis and man pages
watch: Learn Linux TV: Linux Commands for Beginners (playlist)
topics.ai_job: AI is great for quick answers, but the man page is the official truth. A good habit: ask AI, then confirm the option in the man page before using it on a real server.
prompts: What is the difference between which, whereis and type? Give an example.
How do I search inside a man page, and what do the sections 1, 5 and 8 mean?
interview: How do you find where a command's program file is?
What are man page sections?

topics.name: The vi editor
watch: Learn Linux TV: Linux Crash Course (playlist)
read: Rocky Linux book: VI Text Editor
Red Hat blog: An introduction to the vi editor
practice: Built-in practice: type vimtutor on your VM (install with: sudo dnf install vim-enhanced)
topics.ai_job: Servers often have only vi. AI can give you a short cheat sheet for exactly what you need (search, replace, delete lines) and explain a vi error when you get stuck.
prompts: Give me the 15 most useful vi commands for a beginner admin, in a small table.
I'm stuck in vi and can't exit. What keys do I press and why?
interview: How do you save and exit in vi?
How do you search and replace a word in vi?

topics.name: Linux folders: /etc, /var, /home, /opt, /proc
watch: freeCodeCamp: Introduction to Linux, full course
practice: OverTheWire Bandit: learn commands as a game
topics.ai_job: AI can turn your notes into a clean cheat sheet or interview answers. Write your own one-line notes first, then ask AI to check them.
prompts: Check my notes about /etc, /var, /home, /opt and /proc. Correct any mistakes: [paste notes]
Explain /proc in simple words. Why is it called a virtual file system?
interview: What is /proc?
What is the difference between /opt and /usr?

topics.name: GitHub: your first repository
watch: Learn Linux TV: Linux Crash Course (playlist)
practice: GitHub Skills: Introduction to GitHub (free, hands-on)
topics.ai_job: In DevOps jobs, everything (scripts, configs, notes) lives in Git. AI can write your README, explain git errors, and suggest good commit messages. A public repo also shows interviewers your work.
prompts: Write a short README for my GitHub repo 'cloud-admin-journey' where I record my Linux and cloud learning each week.
Explain git add, git commit and git push like I'm a beginner.
interview: What is the difference between Git and GitHub?
What is a commit?
